name: South Indian Bank Ltd
title: South Indian Bank Ltd - 532218 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: South Indian Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 17% YoY to INR378 crore, with record NII of INR1,025 crore and NIM of 3.23%.
summary.overview: Net profit grew 17% YoY to INR378 crore, and net interest income hit a record INR1,025 crore, up 23% YoY and INR110 crore QoQ. NIM recovered to 3.23%, up 28 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY, helped by repricing of high-cost deposits, CASA growth and a 50% cut in bulk deposits. Gross advances grew 17% YoY and gross NPA fell to 1.38%. Non-interest income was soft: core fees fell to INR179 crore from INR191 crore in Q4, and management called this a one-off. Management said the call was the last for MD and CEO P.R. Seshadri, who is leaving.

segments.name: Business loans (MSME)
segments.commentary: Business loans rose to INR14,391 crore from INR12,660 crore; growth was 18% excluding a INR554 crore charge-off. Management said MSME growth was muted versus expectations this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book reached INR24,930 crore, up 43% YoY, with average LTV of 65.25% and average ticket size of INR2.94 lakh. QoQ growth was only about 0.8% because co-lending and portfolio purchases of about INR270 crore ran off after an RBI circular effective April 1.

segments.name: Mortgages, home and auto loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage loans grew 34% YoY, home loans 19% and auto loans 34%, excluding IBPC/DA impact.

segments.name: Corporate book
segments.commentary: Corporate lending grew in Q1 as pricing hardened on short-tenor facilities. Corporate is about 40% of the loan book against a stated long-run target of about 30%.

guidance_outlook: NIM: no numeric guidance. Management believes the rate cycle has turned, so NIM should harden as repo changes pass through on a T+1 basis. Management also said the sharp deposit-repricing gains are unlikely to repeat.
Opex: management expects full-year opex growth of about 5-6% and aims for positive operating leverage for the full year. Q1 did not have positive operating leverage.
Fees: management called the fee decline a one-off. Trade and FX platform is expected to go live by end-September 2026.
Slippage: management expects FY27 slippage of INR500-750 crore, with INR800 crore as the maximum even with West Asia stress. Recoveries are expected at INR800-1,000 crore.
Credit cost: management said the 9 bps Q1 cost is probably generous and could moderate.
ROA: management said ROA should move from 100-110 bps toward 120-125 bps over time. No explicit ROE target was given, and the CEO declined a firm multi-year number.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion restarting on a small scale after about 3 years of freeze; branch count had fallen slightly and is being rebuilt in key locations.
Trade and FX digital platform targeted to go live by end-September 2026, covering FX bookings, LCs, guarantees and export/import bill settlement.

Capital: management plans to grow the balance sheet at market growth plus about 2%, shifting mix toward higher risk-weight retail and MSME assets. Risk density is expected to rise, so CRAR will fall from 19.62% over time.
demand_pricing: Deposit costs fell as high-rate deposits repriced down 40-60 bps between January and June 2026. Average CASA grew 19%, and bulk deposits were cut about 50% YoY.
Asset yields rose 5 bps, helped by mix shift, T-bill-linked corporate pricing and firmer corporate pricing on short-tenor loans. Retail pricing did not move up.

FCNR(B) deposits grew about 6% QoQ. Management expects a large share of inflows in August and September before the scheme closes on September 30. Inflows are unlevered because the bank has no external credit lines or GIFT City entity.
Recoveries of INR179 crore in Q1 against slippages of INR128 crore. Q1 is seasonally weak for recoveries.
SMA-1 and SMA-2 rose about INR80 crore QoQ. Management called it seasonal and said the constituents are reversible.
ECLGS: limit of about INR400 crore, disbursed about INR238 crore, with utilised book of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in cost of deposits and the yield rise on advances, and what is the NIM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: High-rate deposits repriced 40-60 bps, CASA grew, and bulk deposits were halved. Yield gains came from mix shift and T-bill-linked corporate pricing. Management gave no numeric NIM guidance, but expects NIMs to harden if the rate cycle has turned.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex and hiring rise for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Branch rollout is restarting in key locations. Opex growth is expected at about 5-6% for the year, with positive operating leverage targeted for the full year after Q1 lacked it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income soften, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Core fees fell to INR179 crore from INR191 crore, partly from a product renewal fee-charging error that will be fixed. Treasury income fell to INR44 crore and Q1 FY26 PSLC sale income of about INR60 crore did not recur. Management called this an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: Why is corporate share about 40% against a 30% target?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate pricing improved and liquidity was available, so the bank added short-tenor, high-quality corporate loans. Management still intends to reduce corporate exposure over the long run.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost run rate, and what about SMA-1/2 and ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost was 9 bps. Management called that generous and expects moderation. FY27 slippage is seen at INR500-750 crore. Management expects no material NII impact from ECL effective-interest changes.

qa_highlights.question: Is FCNR(B) growth sustainable after June, and what is the landed cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflows are strong and expects most in August-September. Pricing matches domestic rupee liquidity levels. Landed cost was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for excess capital and the ROA and ROE path?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance sheet to grow at market growth plus about 2%, with mix shifting to higher risk-weight retail and MSME. ROA target path is 100-110 bps moving toward 120-125 bps; no firm ROE guidance was given.

risks_watch: Leadership transition: the MD and CEO is leaving, and management declined to commit to multi-year ROA or ROE targets that would bind a successor.
NIM tailwind may fade: management said the sharp deposit-repricing benefit is unlikely to repeat at the same scale.
Corporate exposure at about 40% of the book, above the 30% target, with West Asia uncertainty cited.
Gold loan QoQ growth was only about 0.8% after the RBI circular, and bulk-deal run-off is ongoing.
FCNR(B) inflows depend on the Dubai rep office permissibility and on foreign bank credit lines that have not yet materialised.
SMA-1/2 rose about INR80 crore QoQ; management attributes this to seasonality, but the trend needs monitoring.
Fee income recovery: management has to show that core fees rebound from INR179 crore and that the trade/FX platform goes live by end-September.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, asset quality and capital, but cautious on fees and MSME momentum. The CEO said the rate cycle has turned and avoided numeric NIM and ROE guidance, citing his exit.
key_quotes: And so now we are in a position where our belief is the rate cycle has switched. So it's more likely to increase than to reduce.
We think that the 9 basis points that we currently have is probably on a generous side.
So with respect to fees, my own view is that it's a one-timer. We shouldn't read this as something that is going to last forever.

growth.why: Guidance is for FY27 opex growth of 5-6%, slippage of INR500-750 crore (max INR800 crore) and recoveries of INR800-1,000 crore, plus ROA drifting from 100-110 bps toward 120-125 bps over time; growth is backed only partly by pricing, mix and deposit repricing, with branch expansion small and no explicit revenue or loan growth target given.

mgmt.note: Management said this call was the last for MD and CEO P.R. Seshadri, who is leaving; no successor or growth stance was described in the brief.
